The Present Perfect is often described as a mixture of the past and the present. It is used to talk about an action that happened in the past, or started in the past, but has a relationship to the present situation.
• Our boss has agreed to give us an extension on the report.

In this example, the boss agreed to give an extension in the past, but we don't know when that happened. The exact time is not important, but the consequence in the present is that there is more time to work on the report.

FORM:
You have really impressed our client.
You have made my job easier.
Peter has asked for a week off.
In spoken English, these are the top 10 verbs most frequently used in the Present Perfect.
Example: Our client has agreed to give us an extension on the proposal until Friday.

Janet: Hi, Miranda. Let's keep this meeting fairly brief. What was the outcome of your meeting with Farmani?
Miranda: Encouraging. Farmani has agreed to give us an extension until Friday.
Janet: Good work. You must have impressed him.
Miranda: I believe it's a good sign that we have his confidence.
Janet: Sorry, but I wouldn't bank on it until he has approved the proposal. Well, we have work to do!

Miranda: Yes, but first I have a request.
Janet: Shoot.
Miranda: Peter has requested the week off, if that's alright.
Janet: Could you elaborate? This sounds more like Peter's request than your own.
Miranda: You are right. It is Peter's request due to some family demands. However, it doesn't sound like there's an emergency.

Janet: I'm afraid we have to decline his request. This is a very critical time. Are we in agreement?
Miranda: Yes. I strongly disagree myself. Your refusal has made my job easier.
Janet: Glad to help. Next on the agenda: When do we see Ferdinand?
Miranda: After lunch, if that's alright. Ferdinand sounds ready and eager.
Janet: That's what I like to hear! 12:30 then?

Miranda: Actually, 1:00 would be more convenient. I have a conference call over lunch.
Janet: 1:30 sharp then.
Miranda: I'll let him know. Any other business?
Janet: No. Have a good morning.
Miranda: You too.
